title: Original SimpleHook malformed-data membership and recovery
oracle: Source-reviewed empty/malformed-call, strict object identity, all-duplicate removal, LIFO, nullish-query, null-stored error/repair and NaN literals. Bounded token histories use an independent ordered token list. No actual callback or once wrapper is supplied.

trials.execution: Executed partial malformed-data lifecycle observations against actual SimpleHook sources at 1051710191 and 1051908825 through the generic core Subject: 14 cases, 219 probes per revision, 14 unchanged comparisons; 15 tests passed. A private observer retained 28 full content-addressed records before assertions, covering 42 single-revision executions and 657 probes including repeated baseline runs. All 28 frozen files and all case oracles stayed unchanged. Explicit diagnostic process mode reports isolated:false. No valid callbacks, once wrappers, callback delivery, container or production scheduling acceptance.
trials.dataScope: All registered values are deliberately noncallable data. Callback membership/removal and failed-call recovery are characterized; successful valid-callback or event delivery is not accepted.
trials.returnScope: Actual add returns supplied data when once is not true; actual removeLast returns popped data. These source return boundaries permit object references without argument retention or helper callbacks.
trials.domains: Payload, options, equality and history domains are unbounded. once uses an exact true comparison, not a Boolean input-domain guarantee. once:true is excluded because it returns a function.
trials.lifetimeScope: Each case constructs an actual fresh source class instance in its own worker; no persisted restart, cross-thread or source integration acceptance.

limitations: Only supported gate APIs and static key expressions are inventoried.
Logical work units bound selected AST traversal and resolution, not parser internals or elapsed time; parsing remains source-byte bounded.
Declared fixture-provider boundaries exclude their original resolver implementations and dependencies.
All functions in each dependency module are scanned; exact export and caller reachability is not proven.
Runtime-discovered gates and externally selected code require separate observations.

exclusions: Executed observations cover only selected malformed-data registration/removal and failed-call recovery in fresh realms. They do not establish valid callback delivery, complete input histories or integration behavior.
All callback inputs are malformed noncallable data; valid callback delivery/order/reentrancy/exception handling/once behavior remain unaccepted.
once:true returns a source function and remains blocked: no function snapshot/retention, discard/identity trick, meta/native Function method, fake helper or authority change.
Plain data.$1 matching is a source property-equality characterization, not proof that the data is a genuine once wrapper or callback.
No direct removeIf predicate test, private $2 access, internal property read/mutation, callback fixture, host object/function, async/pending or clock control.
Keys/data/options/histories are unbounded. Zero gate descriptors is not semantic proof or exhaustive input/consumer coverage.
No Banzai/qex integration, provider/account/browser/network/timer, container isolation, service adapter or production authored-suite scheduling proof.
